metadata.title: How did people come up with the early public strategies in the first place?

messages.content:
I was doing RL for about a month of a half. BC saved a lot of training time but didn't seem necessary for a good bot, as improvements were pretty correlated with training time: my fresh RL runs could catch up to my weaker BC runs in an hour or two. I think this describes a lot of the top bots that went the RL+self-play route as well.

I wasn't high on the leaderboard until the end, but that was much more because I finally did a big training run than because of BC. If you have big batch sizes, a competitive league, and a well tuned RL algorithm and model, it will learn quite optimal strategies and continue improving with training.

code and diagrams
I found this part in your repo, it says you tried RL without BC and it plateaued (at a similar level to my attempt :D). What did you change in order for pure RL to be successful?

That was very early on, and excuse the slop, I probably should have cleaned up the repo more. I did not see plateau in elo gain after a combination of improvements:

  1. a better model: lejepa backbone, position-specified targets for movement (moveto(x, y) and pseudo-pathfind, instead of my previous move(direction)), Win/Draw/Loss reward/critic instead of dense or soft-terminal rewards. As well as better market actions allowing more specific trading quantities.
  2. critic warmup on the random model, mostly just saves training time.
  3. a hardness-focused self-play league with screening of historical opponents we are uncertain a about (due to having not played recently), and play against those we think will be the hardest to win against.
  4. sufficient training time at a lower learning rate: after 30-45mins (more when BCing from the top elo games), the from-fresh model improves quite well and catches up to BC+RL.

I found about similar entropy and strategy after awhile.

Strong BC models only started showing up during the last couple of weeks of the competition. Since I had mostly been following public replays and existing solutions, I always wondered: how did people figure out those strategies before BC models were available? This is the GitHub repository for my solution: GitHub repository

I'm also eager to hear from the top teams also.

I will share an observation I had. In this competiton, we can first build a solo bot that plays without an opponent and maximizes its money. We could achieve $200k+ this way. Then add reinforcement learning to react/adapt/challenge opponents.
I had the same question and wait here too !
